models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light NE flow easing to near-calm through 25 Sep - but we're 10 days out, so nothing here applies to the trip itself.
briefing.synopsis: Current picture over the Aeolians is a weak NE-to-N gradient with no organised low or strong high-pressure squeeze in evidence: ECMWF IFS 0.25 and AIFS (both 23 Sep 00Z) with ICON-2i agree on 6-12 kt from 060-070 degrees overnight 22/23 Sep, backing through N by evening on the 23rd. From 24 Sep the flow collapses - 1-3 kt at most islands by midday, direction wandering W to NW - and stays light through 25 Sep with a modest W-SW sea breeze signal of 5-8 kt around midday. Seas fall in step: Filicudi peaks at 2.4 ft total with 2.2 ft swell on 23 Sep, then everything drops to 0.3-0.6 ft by the 25th. The model data ends 29 Sep, so beyond that we have nothing.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: No boats in the water yet; for reference, the rehearsal run scores Portorosa Marina as sheltered on the night of 23 Sep - enclosed basin, all-round shelter, and the choice does not matter there. Portorosa shows 4-5 kt with 0.9-1.4 ft wave in the payload, which is a non-event for a berthed cat. The berth analysis for the actual trip nights cannot be run until those dates come inside the forecast horizon.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Not a departure question yet - the fleet sails on 3 October and the models only reach 29 September. What the rehearsal shows for the coming week is early starts in near-calm air: 06:00 departures with 1-5 kt at most islands through 24-25 Sep, which would be motoring more than sailing. Treat that as a check of the routing logic, not a preview.

cautions: Every leg verdict in this brief comes from a rehearsal against late-September weather. The real trip dates (3-8 Oct) are outside all model horizons - do not plan around these numbers.
ECMWF IFS gusts are interval maxima, so figures like 26-28 kt at Stromboli and Filicudi on 23 and 25 Sep sit against 8-10 kt means. They are an artefact of light air, not a squall signal.

Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli scores only 'workable' even in 7 kt - it is open from every direction and depends entirely on it staying calm. Worth flagging now for trip planning regardless of the eventual forecast.
briefing.confidence_note: Near-term model agreement is good - stability tracking shows mean wind shifts of about 1 kt and 54 degrees of direction wander at 72-120 h lead - but the trip dates lie roughly five days past the end of any available run, so confidence for the voyage itself is effectively nil.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
